target_customer: New York consumers buying and selling event tickets and reservations peer to peer
problem: Classifieds such as Craigslist were slow and untrusted for time sensitive items like tickets. Shout added real time chat and in app payment to each listing.
business_model: Marketplace, with payments handled in app

founders.name: Zachariah Reitano
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in the TechCrunch launch article, which gives no background.

founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and in the TechCrunch launch article, which gives no background.

competitors.what: Classifieds service the article compares to Craigslist

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app with chat and payments is standard engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Ticket resale and classifieds apps were easy to copy and no network effect was shown beyond a New York launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ticket marketplaces such as TickPick and SeatGeek were already running apps by 2014 and 2015 per press releases.

market_need_then: The launch article says users mainly sold concert and Broadway tickets in New York, suggesting demand for quick ticket exchange. No usage figures are given.

branding.domain_note: Used useshout.com, a prefix domain, per the YC page.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and PYMNTS at launch in 2014. No fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage exists but many unrelated apps share the name Shout, so search found mostly other products.

outcome_analysis: Shout launched in New York in August 2014 as a real time classifieds app used mostly for tickets and then went inactive. No shutdown notice or cause was found, so the cause of failure is not public. The generic name and crowded ticket and classifieds markets are context, not stated causes.
